subject.declared_domain: the kuzu graph object published into the estate-report bucket for the estate-report EC2 runner to consume as its blast-radius substrate

methodology.evidence: ⛔ I HAVE NEVER OPENED THIS OBJECT. Its EXISTENCE, SIZE and VINTAGE are MEASURED by head-object; everything about HOW IT IS PRODUCED is read from infra/aws/terraform/estate-report/instance.tf:136-143 @HEAD, which declares it is 'published daily into this same bucket by the early-morning Nessie run and OVERWRITTEN each day'. That is the CONFIG's account of the producer, not an observation of it. 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp~X (73339) measured the same object independently and states the identical limit. DECLARED_OPINIONS IS NULL AND THE REASON IS THAT I NEVER OPENED THE OBJECT: its producer is known only from instance.tf prose, not observed, so any opinion set I listed would be the CONFIG's account of a producer rather than the producer's own choices.
methodology.owner: estate-report pipeline owner -- 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps lane per EC2 ownership
methodology.how: Per instance.tf, the early-morning Nessie run publishes the canonical kuzu graph to this key; the runner drops it at <clone>/infra/aws/globgrph/kuzu_nessie_db, which is where comp-blast resolves it with no flag. Placing the file IS the integration.

cadence.evidence: DESIRED vs APPLIED, and they disagree. DECLARED: instance.tf:136-138 says published DAILY and OVERWRITTEN each day. MEASURED: head-object returns LastModified 2026-08-06T21:49:50Z -- 20 DAYS before carding. ⛔ The config's own comment anticipates a MISSING object ('A MISSING OBJECT MUST READ AS INSTRUMENT_FAILED, NEVER AS no blast radius') and does NOT cover a STALE one, which is present and answers.

persistence.evidence: head-object: ContentLength 51,068,928, VersionId 1qzIq4TIzcemaprP8Rqq.3AaYvpnMy2O, ServerSideEncryption AES256. A VersionId is present, so the bucket is versioned and an overwrite would retain prior bytes.

coverage.evidence: ⛔ COVERAGE IS NOT MEASURABLE WITHOUT OPENING THE OBJECT, AND I DID NOT OPEN IT. The 51,068,928-byte size is measured; a node/edge count is not, because reading it would mean downloading and opening a kuzu database whose contents I make no claim about.

coverage.denominator_absent_reason: The object was never opened by this lane. Size is measured (51,068,928 bytes) but a row count requires downloading and opening the database, which was out of scope for a card whose subject is the published artifact. Stating this rather than inferring a count from the byte size, which would be a guess dressed as a measurement.
explicitly_out: anything written to the warehouse after 2026-08-06T21:49:50Z

key.evidence: Not opened, so the internal key space is not observed. IF it is a copy of the canonical projection its key space would be CloudNode.node_id -- but that is exactly the inference this card refuses to make, because a 51MB object and an 82MB object are not the same object and the difference is unexplained.  || KEY_EXPRESSION ABSENT: the object was never opened -- the card's identity_space is literally UNOBSERVED, so no expression can be stated without inventing one. NULL payload with basis absent is the honest row, and it is what v3 legalises for exactly this case.
key.identity_space: UNOBSERVED -- the object was not opened

failure_mode.evidence: EXERCISED on the retrieval path, which is the failure this store's CONSUMER actually meets: head-object on a key that cannot exist returns 'An error occurred (404) when calling the HeadObject operation: Not Found'. LOUD and distinguishable from the rc=0 + ContentLength of the real key in the same session. ⛔ BUT THE CONSUMER-SIDE FAILURE IS NOT THE 404: instance.tf states a missing object must read as INSTRUMENT_FAILED. The measured condition is a 20-day-STALE object, which returns rc=0 and full bytes -- so the runner receives a confident answer about a 20-day-old world, and NOTHING in the retrieval distinguishes that from a fresh one.
failure_mode.returns_on_failure: 404 Not Found on absence; on staleness, a complete and successful read of old bytes
silent_degrade_paths: a stale object returns rc=0 with full bytes, so the declared INSTRUMENT_FAILED path never triggers and blast radius is computed against a 20-day-old graph

verdict.why: The store EXISTS and is retrievable, and its absence would be loud. It is UNSOUND because its declared cadence and its measured vintage disagree by 20 days on a DAILY contract, and the disagreement is invisible to its consumer: the config anticipates a missing object but not a stale one, so a successful read of 20-day-old bytes is indistinguishable from a correct read. Three of seven rows additionally rest on inference because the object was never opened, which this card records rather than papers over.
blocking_defects: declared daily cadence vs 20-day measured vintage
staleness is invisible to the consumer -- the INSTRUMENT_FAILED path covers absence only
coverage and key space unmeasured because the object was not opened
